description: Capabilities granted to every desktop widget window. The same narrow set the HUD overlay gets, and for the same reason: a chromeless window floating above everything, one per widget, is the easiest surface here to mistake for something it is not. A widget shows a number, moves itself and closes itself — so it gets dragging, cursor pass-through, always-on-top, close and the event channel the frames and its own configuration arrive on. It may also enumerate monitors, read-only, because a widget has to know which screens exist before it can say which one it is on (a denied `availableMonitors` rejects rather than answers, and the widget silently lands on one screen). No store, no filesystem, no dialogs, no process control, and no set-position: a widget is placed by Rust when it is created and afterwards by the user's mouse, never by the page.
